meta.name: TPU95A
meta.description: TPU 95A (Shore-A 95) flexible filament. Density and compression regime pulled from the basketball work (rho 1210 kg/m3, compression modulus ~38 MPa, resilience 0.43, elongation > 560%); tensile/strength/creep/fatigue/service block migrated from material_db.json (Ultimaker TPU 95A datasheet). Tensile and compression moduli differ by loading mode — both are carried, not conflated. Density disagrees between the two sources (1210 vs 1220) — see conflicts.

sn_curve.note: engineering rule of thumb (~1e6-cycle allowable = ultimate x 0.4); elastomers tolerate cyclic strain well. NOT a measured S-N curve

anisotropy.model: scalar-tier direction heuristic (production_check.py): across-layer (Z) tensile strength / in-plane (XY) strength; elastomers bond layers well so the ratio is high (0.75)

sources.physical.density_kg_m3: basketball work: rho 1.21e-3 g/mm3 = 1210 kg/m3 (compression-regime design value)
sources.mechanical.youngs_modulus_pa: material_db.json TPU95A.youngs_pa = 2.6e7 (Ultimaker TPU 95A TENSILE modulus 26 MPa; 95A moduli vary 26-90 MPa between brands)
sources.mechanical.poisson: typical near-incompressible elastomer ~0.48 (material_db.json has no poisson); provided for FEA
sources.mechanical.sn_curve: material_db.json TPU95A.fatigue_knockdown 0.4 (rule of thumb, not a measured curve)
sources.mechanical.compression_modulus_pa: basketball work: compression modulus ~38 MPa (loading mode differs from the 26 MPa tensile modulus)
sources.mechanical.elongation_at_break_pct: material_db.json TPU95A source (Ultimaker ~580% elongation); consistent with the basketball '> 560%'
sources.thermal.tg_or_melt_c: TPU softens near its service limit; ~60 C (literature/typical)
sources.thermal.conductivity_w_mk: typical TPU ~0.2 W/mK (literature); no current analyzer consumes it
sources.thermal.specific_heat_j_kgk: typical TPU ~1800 J/kgK (literature); no current analyzer consumes it
sources.thermal.cte_per_k: typical elastomer linear CTE ~150e-6 /K (literature); no current analyzer consumes it
sources.thermal.softening_c: softening_c = conservative softening allowable for sustained-load design: the LOW end of min(Tg, HDT-B 0.45 MPa) across cited brand TDS values for this material class (degC). TPU95A: 45 C = HDT-B class of printed flexibles: NinjaFlex 85A TDS HDT 0.45 MPa = 44 C https://ninjatek.com/wp-content/uploads/NinjaFlex-TDS.pdf ; NinjaTek Cheetah 95A TDS HDT 0.45 = 49 C (printed specimens) https://ninjatek.com/wp-content/uploads/Cheetah-TDS.pdf ; Covestro: TPU has no sharp softening point and creeps under load from ~45-50 C. Bambu TPU 95A HF TDS lists Tg/Vicat/HDT as N/A https://store.bblcdn.eu/s8/default/16df21baf482453999b3dbb61cc110e7/Bambu_TPU_95A_HF_Technical_Data_Sheet.pdf
sources.thermal.conductivity_w_mk (2026-07-30 ve: record 0.2 confirmed at the conservative end: Covestro Desmopan 0.20-0.25 W/mK @20 C (falling to 0.17-0.20 @80 C) https://solutions.covestro.com/en/highlights/articles/theme/product-technology/thermal-properties-tpu ; Kruse TPU 0.18-0.25

conflicts.note: basketball work uses 1210; material_db uses 1220. ~0.8% drift. Canonical = the basketball-validated design value; material_db 1220 retained here for visibility. No in-repo consumer currently reads TPU density from a record, so this changes no shipped result.

conflicts.other_source: basketball work: compression modulus ~38 MPa (stored as mechanical.compression_modulus_pa)
conflicts.note: NOT a bug: youngs_modulus_pa is the TENSILE modulus (26 MPa, datasheet convention shared with the other records); the 38 MPa figure is the COMPRESSION modulus and lives in mechanical.compression_modulus_pa. A 95A TPU legitimately has different tensile vs compression moduli. Surfaced so a consumer picks the modulus for its loading mode.

conflicts.other_source: Covestro Desmopan cp 1.45-1.70 J/gK @20 C https://solutions.covestro.com/en/highlights/articles/theme/product-technology/thermal-properties-tpu ; Ho et al. 2010 neat TPU 1500 J/kgK https://www.hindawi.com/journals/jnm/2010/583234/ ; Kruse 1500-2000
conflicts.note: record's 1800 sits above the sourced 20 C band (1450-1700; Covestro reaches 1700-1900 only at 80 C). 1500 would be the conservative (faster-heating) RT value; changing a canonical is a human physics decision — surfaced, not silently overwritten.

conflicts.other_source: NinjaTek Cheetah 95A TDS Tg = -24 C (DSC) https://ninjatek.com/wp-content/uploads/Cheetah-TDS.pdf (NinjaFlex 85A: -35 C)
conflicts.note: the record's 60 is a softening/service-class number, not a DSC Tg: TPU's actual glass transition is far below room temperature. Use thermal.softening_c (45) for heat gates; 60 matches the 'max recommended service' class (NinjaFlex TDS says 66).
